residual_risks: This spike maps the task's five conceptual categories (metadata, content, indexes, cache, replicas) onto three real, distinct backends (PostgreSQL, TypeDB, Qdrant); it does not stand up five physically separate systems, since the property being proven -- DELETION_INCOMPLETE until every independent store confirms absence, never a false DELETED -- is fully exercised by three backends and does not strengthen with a fourth or fifth.

The saga orchestrator itself (run_deletion_saga) is generic and accepts any object satisfying the DeletionTarget protocol; only the concrete PostgreSQL/TypeDB/Qdrant targets are new sealed-adapter-reusing code -- a synthetic LyingTarget/UnreachableTarget is used only in two pure unit/contract tests of the orchestrator's own classification logic, never as a substitute for real backend evidence (both real end-to-end tests use exclusively real backends).

The real fault-injection drill targets TypeDB specifically (pause/unpause); PostgreSQL and Qdrant were not independently fault-injected in this task's evidence, since OCOR-DEV-0016 (PostgreSQL concurrency/failure) and OCOR-DEV-0023 (Qdrant partition isolation, with its own fault-tolerant design) already sealed real fault-injection evidence for those two backends independently.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: The TypeDB pause/unpause cycle recovers in a finally block before the test's own assertions run; the Qdrant fixture tears down its self-provisioned container in a finally block regardless of test outcome. Verified directly by the post-run check that no self-provisioned Qdrant containers were left behind, that TypeDB was genuinely healthy again (confirmed via a direct HTTP call past the Docker healthcheck's own settle delay), and that the persistent 11-service stack remained healthy across 4 consecutive full test-suite runs including 4 real pause/unpause cycles. The CI provisioning fix was rehearsed end-to-end locally (start, health-wait, real endpoint check, teardown) on alternate ports before being added to any workflow.
